headline: Adopted a ban on data centers in industrial zones and approved a $169,000 contract for a Factory Pond well field study.
summary: Veolia Water gave an update on drought conditions and possible new well sites. The council set hearings on a Peace Dale Preserve special management district at 371 Rose Hill Road and on a harbor management plan update, and it referred a pool safety cover proposal to the Planning Board. It also approved a $19,908.91 fiber contract for the new high school, four board appointments, and routine license renewals.
decisions: Approved sealing the minutes of the closed executive session on real property, unanimously.
Approved reappointing Charlene Traynum to the Housing Authority of South Kingstown, unanimously.
Approved appointing Joe “Tiger” Patrick to the Saugatucket Veterans’ Memorial Park Commission, unanimously.
Approved appointing David Cote to the Canvassing Authority as Alternate Member (R), unanimously.
Approved appointing Paul McConnell to the Canvassing Authority as Alternate Member (D), unanimously.
Approved a $19,908.91 fiber services contract with Sertex Broadband Solutions, with a $3,000 contingency, unanimously.
Approved extending the 2023 bid award to United Site Services Northeast for portable restroom services for 2027, unanimously.
Approved Rhode Island Energy and Verizon New England petition to install pole P15-1 on Narragansett Avenue East, unanimously.
Approved Rhode Island Energy and Verizon New England petition to install joint pole P3-1 on School Street, unanimously.
Approved a $5,000.68 tax abatement under Tax Abatement Request No. 669, unanimously.
Approved victualling license renewals for four Wakefield businesses, unanimously.
Approved a Shellfish and Farm Produce Peddler License for Stoney Acres Farm, unanimously.
Approved a Farm Retail Sales License renewal for Wicked Rhody LLC, unanimously.
Approved a Tourist Accommodations License renewal for Sheppard’s Campus Bed & Breakfast, unanimously.
Approved advertising a public hearing on renewal of the Elite Indoor Gun Range license at 371 Rose Hill Road, unanimously.
Approved a CivicPlus website contract renewal of $12,008.26, with a 3-year renewal option, unanimously.
Adopted zoning amendments prohibiting data centers in Industrial Zones, unanimously.
Approved amending the charge of the Saugatucket Veterans’ Memorial Park Commission to broaden board membership requirements, unanimously.
Approved advertising a public hearing on the July 2026 update to the Harbor Management Plan, unanimously.
Approved advertising a hearing on zoning amendments to establish the Peace Dale Preserve Special Management District at 371 Rose Hill Road, unanimously.
Approved the Town Manager signing a grant agreement with the federal Health Resources and Services Administration for a new ambulance and equipment, unanimously.
Approved the Town Manager signing a subrecipient agreement with Restore America’s Estuaries for stormwater work in the Saugatucket River watershed, unanimously.
Approved a contract with GZA GeoEnvironmental, not to exceed $169,000 including a $35,000 contingency, for the Factory Pond well field study, unanimously.
Referred a proposed ordinance amendment on pool safety covers to the Planning Board and Town Solicitor’s office; Council Member Wegimont voted no.

REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 26, 2026 
 
1 
At a REGULAR SESSION of the Town Council of the Town of South Kingstown, County of 
Washington, in the State of Rhode Island held at the Town Hall, in and for said Town on the 26th day 
of October 2026 at 6:33 PM. 
 
 PRESENT: Rory H. McEntee, President  
  Michael K. Marran, Vice President 
Deborah D. Bergner 
Patricia A. Alley 
Jay G. Wegimont 
 
1. A. CLOSED EXECUTIVE SESSION 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to recess to Closed Executive Session pursuant to §42 -46-5(a)(5) 
pertaining to discussions or considerations related to the acquisition or lease of real property for 
public purposes, or of the disposition of publicly held property wherein advanced public information 
would be detrimental to the interest of the public 
 
Regular Session is reconvened at 7:40 PM. 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to seal the minutes of Closed Executive Session pursuant to §42-46-
5(a)(5) pertaining to discussions or considerations related to the acquisition or lease of real property 
for public purposes, or of the disposition of publicly held property wherein advanced public 
information would be detrimental to the interest of the public 
 
It is noted that no votes were taken in Executive Session. 
 
 
Emily R. Houle 
Town Clerk
REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 26, 2026 
 
2 
At a REGULAR SESSION of the Town Council of the Town of South Kingstown, County of 
Washington, in the State of Rhode Island held at the Town Hall, in and for said Town on the 26th day 
of October 2026 at 7:44 PM. 
 
 PRESENT: Rory H. McEntee, President  
  Michael K. Marran, Vice President 
Deborah D. Bergner 
Patricia A. Alley 
Jay G. Wegimont 
 
 
2. REGULAR SESSION  
 
A. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  
 
The Pledge of Allegiance is given. 
 
B. LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT  
 
The Land Acknowledgement Statement is read. 
 
3. ROLL CALL 
 
Roll Call is taken. Council Vice President Marran is absent. 
 
4. APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF PREVIOUS MEETINGS 
 
A. Regular Session: UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: that the minutes of the Regular Session held 
on October 13, 2026 are accepted, approved, and placed on file. 
 
C. Joint Special Session: UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: that the minutes of the Joint Special 
Session with the Town Council and School Committee  held on October 13, 2026 are accepted, 
approved, and placed on file. 
 
5. INTERVIEWS 
 
A. The Council interviews Charlene Traynum relative to her interest in being reappointed to the 
South Kingstown Housing Authority. 
 
B. The Council interviews Paul McConnell relative to his interest in being appointed to the South 
Kingstown Canvassing Authority. 
 
C. The Council interviews David Cote relative to his interest in being appointed to the South 
Kingstown Canvassing Authority. 
 
D. Steven Stewart is not in attendance to be interviewed. 
 
E. The Council interviews Joe “Tiger” Patrick relative to his interest in being appointed to the 
Saugatucket Veterans’ Memorial Park Commission.
REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 26, 2026 
 
3 
6. APPOINTMENTS 
 
A. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to reappoint Charlene Traynum to the Housing Authority of South 
Kingstown for a term to expire October 2031. 
 
B. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to appoint Joe “Tiger” Patrick to Saugatucket Veterans’ Memorial 
Park Commission for a term to expire October 2031. 
 
C. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to appoint David Cote to the Canvassing Authority as the Alternate 
Member (R) to fill a term to expire March 2027.  
 
D. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to appoint Paul McConnell to the Canvassing Authority as the 
Alternate Member (D) for a term to expire March 2032. 
 
The Town Manager’s Report 12A is brought forward. 
 
TOWN MANAGER’S REPORT 
 
A. Joseph Keough, legal counsel for Veolia Water, introduces Chris Jacobs , Manager of 
Veolia’s Rhode Island Operations, and reviews his previous appearances at Town Council meetings. 
 
Chris Jacobs reports on aquifer recharge levels and notes that the drought advisory is in place for 
another month before the odd/even water ban may be lifted. He reviews criteria that the RI Drought 
Steering Committee uses to determine drought stages and forecast data used by Veolia for water 
restrictions. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to Veolia’s communication with the Town. 
 
Richard Bourbonnais, Public Services Director, reviews data received from Veolia.  
 
Discussion ensues relative to Access to Public Records Act (APRA) regulations and water ban 
related requests.  
 
Chris Jacobs notes that Veolia is researching potential well sites. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to water ban enforcement by Veolia, the potential timeline to have new 
wells become active, and future communication efforts between Veolia and the Town.  
 
7. CONSENT AGENDA 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to approve the Consent Agenda as indicated by (CA) on same with the 
exception of Consent Agenda A. 
 
(CA) B. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an award of contract to Sertex Broadband 
Solutions, 22 Center Parkway, Plainfield, CT 06374 for fiber services in the amount of $19,908.91 
with a contingency of $3,000 as described in a memorandum from the Director of Technology to the 
Town Manager dated October 13, 2026 and titled “Fiber Extension for New High School.” 
 
(CA) C. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an extension of an award of bid originally 
granted on January 23, 2023, to United Site Services Northeast, Inc., 118 Flanders Road,
REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 26, 2026 
 
4 
Westborough, MA 01581 for Portable Restroom Services, at the 2026 unit prices bid, for the 2027 
calendar year, and as further described in a memorandum from the Leisure Services Director to the 
Town Manager dated October 16, 2026 and entitled, "Bid Extension Recommendation – Portable 
Restroom Services." 
 
(CA) D. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant the Petition #15080958 of Rhode Island Energy 
and Verizon New England to install pole P15-1 to hold a pole top antenna that is currently on P15 on 
the south side of Narragansett Avenue East, approximately 367 feet east of Narragansett Avenue 
East and Peckham Drive intersection, and to use the public ways named for the purposes stated in 
said petition, that the work be done to the satisfaction of the Director of Public Services and 
notification to Town for municipal utility mark -out prior to pole setting, an d that this approval is 
conditioned upon the removal of all existing double poles along the entire length of Narragansett 
Avenue East prior to new pole(s) placement; and any new double poles created as part of this 
request be removed within sixty (60) calendar days of new pole(s) placement. Said petition is further 
described in a memorandum from the Public Services Director to the Town Manager dated October 
15, 2026 and entitled “Rhode Island Energy Pole Setting Request – Pole P15-1 Narragansett Avenue 
East." Book 6, Page 37. 
 
 
(CA) E. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant the Petition #15067474 of Rhode Island Energy 
and Verizon New England to install Joint Pole P3-1 on the south side of School Street on Town of 
South Kingstown property located at 36 School Street (AP 57-1, Lot 111) for the Union Fire District, 
Station 3 - Forestry Fire Station Renovation Project to provide an underground distribution system 
over, under, through, across, and upon Grantor's Land (see attached easement), that the work be 
done to the satisfaction of the Director of Public Services and notification to the Town for municipal 
utility mark-out prior to pole setting, and that this approval is cond itioned upon the removal of all 
existing double poles along the entire length of School Street prior to new pole(s) placement; and 
any new double poles created as part of this request be removed within sixty (60) calendar days of 
new pole(s) placement. Said petition is further described in a memorandum from the Public Services 
Director to the Town Manager dated October 21, 2026 and entitled, "Rhode Island  Energy Pole 
Setting Request - Pole P3-1 at 36 School Street." Book 6, Page 38. 
 
(CA) F. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize the Town Assessor to abate taxes in the 
amount of $5,000.68, as shown on Tax Abatement Request No. 669. 
 
(CA) G. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant Victualling Licenses to the following; Renewals: 
 
Justin Fontaine Restaurants LLC d/b/a Meldgie’s Rivers Edge Café, 406 Main Street, Wakefield, RI 
02879. Application by Justin Fontaine, Owner. License No. 90662. 
Justin Fontaine Restaurants LLC d/b/a Arabella’s Coffee House, 406 Main Street, Wakefield, RI 
02879. Application by Justin Fontaine, Owner. License No. 91159. 
PB PVD SoCo LLC d/b/a Playa Bowls RI, 36 South County Commons Way, Wakefield, RI 02879. 
Application by Michael Walsh, Partner. License No. 89681. 
Coastal Vitality LLC d/b/a The Fresh Monkee, 540 Kingstown Road, Wakefield, RI 02879. Application 
by Andrew Simmons, Owner. License No. 92285.
REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 26, 2026 
 
5 
(CA) H. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant a Shellfish and Farm Produce Peddler License for 
the year beginning December 1, 2026 to Stoney Acres Farm d/b/a Stoney Acres Farm, 140 Stoney 
Acres Way, Wakefield, RI 02879. Application by Linda Stedman, Co-Owner. Renewal; License No. 
59131. 
 
(CA) I. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant a Farm Retail Sales License for the year beginning 
December 1, 2026, to Wicked Rhody LLC d/b/a Wicked Rhody, West Kingston, RI 02892. Application 
by Brian Hallene, Managing Member. Renewal; License No. 94411. 
 
(CA) J. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant a Tourist Accommodations License for the year 
beginning December 1, 2026 to Sheppard’s Campus Bed & Breakfast d/b/a Sheppard’s Campus 
Bed & Breakfast,16 Campus Avenue, Wakefield, RI 02879. Application by David Sheppard, Owner. 
Renewal; License No. 61883. 
 
(CA) K. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize the Town Clerk to advertise for Order of Notice 
a Public Hearing relative to an application for renewal of an Indoor Shooting Range License in 
accordance with the South Kingstown Town Code, Chapter 9 Licenses and Miscellaneous Business 
Regulation, Article IV Indoor Shooting Ranges, Sec. 9-158 Term of License, Renewal. Application 
by IDGR15, LLC d/b/a Elite Indoor Gun Range, by Mark A. Fay, Member for property located at 371 
Rose Hill Road, Wakefield, RI 02879 and designated as Assessor’s Plat 33, Lot 30, consisting of 
121.57 acres. 
 
(CA) A. Lori Fox, Director of Technology, reviews a request for contract renewal of CivicPlus 
software. She notes ongoing efforts to make the Town’s website more dynamic from a cell phone or 
tablet. 
 
Discussion ensues and it is 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize a contract renewal to CivicPlus, 302 South 4th Street, Suite 
500, Manhattan, KS 66502 for Website Central in the amount of $12,008.26 with a 3-year renewal 
option not to exceed a ten percent (10%) increase over the prior year as described in a memorandum 
from the Director of Technology to the Town Manager dated October 13, 2026 and titled, “Website 
Contract Renewal.” 
 
9. PUBLIC COMMENTS – 30 Minutes 
 
Council President McEntee invites residents to come forward with comments. 
 
Jim O’Neill comments on Massachusetts ballot question #8 regarding recreational marijuana, the 
resignation of RI Democratic Party Chair Liz Beretta-Perik, and statewide politics. 
 
Tiger Patrick recognizes Police Chief Matthew Moynihan for his contributions to the Town and thanks 
him for his service. 
 
Dorald Beasley comments on the upcoming Council President election, additional signage for Rose 
Hill Transfer Station on Route 138 (Mooresfield Road), the High School Building Project, and code 
of conduct for Town employees. 
 
Lucas Murray, Deputy Town Manager, responds.
REGULAR SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 26, 2026 
 
6 
Bob Trager comments on the state of the world. 
 
10. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
A. Notice having been duly given, a Public Hearing is held to consider proposed amendments 
to the Town's Zoning Ordinance, Article 3. Use Regulations, Section 301. Schedule of Use 
Regulations Table., Appendix A. Use Code Descriptions, to prohibit data centers in Industrial Zones, 
as requested by Council Vice President Marran, as follows: 
 
Proposed Amendments to the Town Code Zoning Ordinance 
Appendix A – Zoning Ordinance 
 
***** 
Article 3. Use Regulations. 
Sec. 301.- Schedule of Use Regulations Table. 
Amend as follows: 
[table on following page] 
* * * 
Appendix A. – Use Code Descriptions 
Amend as follows: 
 7.0 INDUSTRIAL 
80 Data Center 
 A room, building, structure, facility, or group of facilities designed, constructed, 
or operated as a principal use for the primary purpose of housing computer 
systems, servers, network equipment, and associated infrastructure for the 
storage, processing, transmission, or management of digital data or 
applications, at a scale and intensity substantially greater than that customarily 
associated with general office, institutional, commercial, or industrial uses.  This 
term includes facilities supporting enterprise computing, colocation services, 
cloud computing, artificial intelligence processing, edge computing, or similar 
high-intensity computing operations, whether operated for a single user or 
multiple users, and whether permanent, modular, or temporary in nature.  This 
term does not include server rooms or information technology infrastructure that 
is customarily incidental and subordinate to another permitted principal use.

11. NEW BUSINESS 
 
A. The Town Clerk reviews the history of the Saugatucket Veterans’ Memorial Park Commission 
and proposed amendments to the board charge. 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to amend the charge of the Saugatucket Veterans' Memorial Park 
Commission to provide for broader requirements for board membership, as detailed in a 
memorandum from the Town Clerk to the Town Manager  dated October 22, 2026 titled, 
“Saugatucket Veterans’ Memorial Park Commission.” 
 
The Town Solicitor reviews a request for an Order of Notice to establish the Peace Dale Preserve 
Special Management District.  
 
Discussion ensues and it is 
 
B. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize the Town Clerk to advertise for Order of Notice a
